title: The five-layer iterated confinement tower as zero-counterterm algebraic renormalization
html:
Iterating functorial column promotion produces a five-layer physical tower \mathcal{L}_0 \to \mathcal{L}_1 \to \mathcal{L}_2 \to \mathcal{L}_3 \to \mathcal{L}_4 governed at each step by a single dimensionless adiabatic ratio \eta_k = \|V_{k+1}\| / \Delta_k evaluated from (m_e, q_0) without fitted counterterms:

Transition Confined motifs promoted Unperturbed gap \Delta_k Next-layer coupling \|V_{k+1}\| Adiabatic ratio \eta_k Physical regime
\mathcal{L}_0 \to \mathcal{L}_1 Elementary B_3 ribbon words \mapsto colour-singlet hadrons (p, n, \pi) m_p(q_0) \approx 938.27\,\mathrm{MeV} Radiative QED dressing \alpha m_p 7.30 \times 10^{-3} Electroweak / QED isospin splitting
\mathcal{L}_1 \to \mathcal{L}_2 Nucleons (p,n) \mapsto bound nuclei (Z, N_{\mathrm{nuc}}) m_p(q_0) \approx 938.27\,\mathrm{MeV} B({}^{12}\mathrm{C})/12 \approx 7.68\,\mathrm{MeV} 8.19 \times 10^{-3} 1\%–5\% EMC structure-function shift without quark deconfinement [aubert-emc1983]
\mathcal{L}_2 \to \mathcal{L}_3 Frozen nuclei (Z,N_{\mathrm{nuc}}) \mapsto neutral atoms and ions (Z, N_e) B({}^{12}\mathrm{C})/12 \approx 7.68\,\mathrm{MeV} \mathrm{Ry} = \frac{1}{2}\alpha^2 m_e \approx 13.61\,\mathrm{eV} 1.77 \times 10^{-6} Complete nuclear conservation across ambient chemistry
\mathcal{L}_3 \to \mathcal{L}_4 Closed-core atoms \mapsto covalent molecules and reaction networks \mathrm{C}(1s) core \approx 442\,\mathrm{eV} (\mathrm{Ry} \approx 13.61\,\mathrm{eV}) Valence bond \approx \frac{1}{3}\mathrm{Ry} (k_B T_{298} \approx 0.0257\,\mathrm{eV}) 1.03 \times 10^{-2} (5.67 \times 10^{-3}) Frozen atomic cores in covalent and thermal chemistry

Zero-counterterm algebraic renormalization versus continuum effective field theory

In Wilsonian renormalization [wilson1971] and Weinberg chiral nuclear effective field theory [weinberg1990], integrating out ultraviolet momentum shells generates an infinite tower of non-renormalizable operators whose low-energy constants must be refitted at each scale. Here, passing from \mathcal{L}_k to \mathcal{L}_{k+1} restricts the ambient braid-Hecke state space onto the finite motif subspace via discrete disentangling projections analogous to entanglement renormalization [vidal2007] and polygraphic normal-form coherence [squier1987, lafont2003, guiraud-malbos2012, guiraud-malbos2018]. Whenever \eta_k < 1, Theorem guarantees that intra-motif fission channels remain strictly endothermic without introducing empirical counterterms.

Cross-layer deconfinement thresholds (\eta_k \to 1)

Conversely, part (3) of Theorem predicts the exact threshold at which extreme thermodynamic potentials reopen a frozen lower layer. Across \mathcal{L}_3 \to \mathcal{L}_2, a degenerate relativistic electron sea supplies perturbation \delta_V = -E_{F,e} to inverse beta capture p + e^- \to n + \nu_e, flipping (m_n - m_p) - E_{F,e} < 0 above the critical electron Fermi energy

  E_{F,e}^* = m_n - m_p = 1.29333\,\mathrm{MeV}
  \qquad
  \bigl(p_{F,e}^* c = 1.18810\,\mathrm{MeV},\;\; n_e^* = 7.3719 \times 10^{30}\,\mathrm{cm}^{-3}\bigr),

marking neutronization in white-dwarf cores and neutron-star outer crusts; at still higher baryon chemical potentials \mu_B \sim \Delta_1, \eta_1 \to 1 reopens \mathcal{L}_2 \to \mathcal{L}_1 nucleon deconfinement.
